origins: Misheard answers, bumping into things, loud responses, and repeated requests can mortify us. We may fear that friends are ashamed to be seen with us.
teaches: “Man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” “Love… does not boast, it is not proud… it keeps no account of wrongs” (1 Corinthians 13:4–5). True friends laugh with you, not at you, and stand by you. “A friend loves at all times” (Proverbs 17:17). God is not embarrassed by you: “The LORD your God is among you; He is mighty to save. He will rejoice over you with gladness.”
errors: Believing I am either smooth or embarrassing.
Feeling embarrassed and concluding that I embarrass others.
questions: What have my friends actually said or done?
Who stays close despite awkward moments?
What would I do if my friend were in my place?
How could humor and honesty help?
What does God feel toward me?
What is one outing I could try?
truth: God rejoices over me, and true friends do not leave over awkward moments. I can be honest about my loss, laugh when it helps, and keep showing up.
hw_truths: A friend loves at all times.
Love keeps no record of wrongs.
log: Each week, note one outing or visit.
actions: Mention your loss lightly at the start.
prayer: Lord, I fear embarrassing others. Remind me that You rejoice over me, and give me friends who stay. Amen.
